name: Parlange Plantation House

dates.altered: The survey says the rear gallery was added and the dining room brought out to fill the first small rear porch, giving the double break to the rear roof; the original cypress shingles replaced with asbestos except on the east side (HABS LA-34).
dates.note: Four statements of the date and they do not agree: the NHL nomination says 'erected about 1750'; the Wikipedia infobox 'c. 1750 (disputed)'; the node's exemplar c. 1750 with fabric analysis arguing for c. 1830-40; and the Koch-era HABS data page itself 'Between 1830 and 1840', adding 'Judging from the details of the interior, the house was erected between 1830 and 1840' and allowing that 'in the 30's an older house was remodeled'. Recorded as the register and node have it; the survey's reading stands beside it unedited.

refs.title: National Register nomination form, Parlange Plantation House (NPGallery)
refs.note: Its statement of significance: 'The Parlange Plantation House, erected about 1750, is the finest and least altered example of a large French colonial plantation house in the United States. It is a classic example of a two-story raised-cottage type of house as it developed in the lower Mississippi Valley.'
